candidates.title: A Spatio-Temporal Expert Prefetching Framework for Efficient MoE-based LLM Inference
candidates.reason: Directly targets MoE expert-loading latency with spatio-temporal prediction and hardware-supported prefetching, matching the repository's expert prefetch/offload focus. The primary-source abstract reports strong cross-layer/token predictability and substantial performance/energy gains, making it a high-value candidate for full research.

candidates.title: Speculating Experts Accelerates Inference for Mixture-of-Experts
candidates.reason: Uses internal representations to speculate future MoE experts so CPU-GPU expert transfers overlap with computation, directly relevant to memory-constrained expert offload and prefetch. It differs from ordinary cache-only methods by allowing speculative expert execution to avoid refetching after router resolution.

candidates.title: Multi-stage Flow Scheduling for LLM Serving
candidates.reason: Addresses network contention across reusable KV retrieval, collective communication, and prefill-to-decode transfer in disaggregated serving. Its stage-aware flow scheduler is a strong adjacent networking/scheduling candidate and reports evaluation on an 8-server, 32-GPU testbed plus simulation.

candidates.title: OServe: Accelerating LLM Serving via Spatial-Temporal Workload Orchestration
candidates.reason: Introduces workload-aware heterogeneous deployment and adaptive deployment switching for spatially and temporally heterogeneous serving traffic. It is relevant to dynamic placement and scheduling, and the primary-source abstract reports up to 2x performance improvement on real-world traces.

candidates.title: NVLLM: A 3D NAND-Centric Architecture Enabling Edge on-Device LLM Inference
candidates.reason: A storage-centric inference architecture that makes 3D NAND an active part of edge LLM execution, closely aligned with the repository's SSD/NVMe and hierarchical-memory emphasis. It is particularly valuable for comparing conventional SSD offload against compute-near-flash designs.

discovery_stats.query_summary: Candidate inventory was below the critical watermark, so discovery rotated away from the preceding KV-centric axis. Primary-source searches targeted MoE expert prediction/prefetch, GPU/runtime and disaggregated-network scheduling, and storage-centric inference architectures. Seven plausible papers were lightweight-screened; five strong candidates were retained for Actions-side final dedupe and research-job materialization.
discovery_stats.next_axis_hint: After Actions-side dedupe, next discovery should favor citation expansion from accepted expert-prefetch papers and adjacent OS/DBMS memory-management or I/O-scheduling work rather than repeat the same generic MoE queries.
